automated_review.mechanism: The revocation-check phase looks up CRLs by the certificate's subject name instead of its issuer name, so the CRL that actually lists revoked serials (indexed by issuer) is never found, causing revoked certificates to pass validation.
automated_review.reason: The comment for the second lookup states it must 'retrieve a CRL corresponding to the _issuer_ of the current certificate in order to check for revocation,' yet the pre-fix code passes `subject`. CRLs are indexed in the store by their issuer name (the CA that signed the CRL), which equals the checked certificate's issuer, not its subject. Consequently the revocation loop operates on an empty/incorrect CRL set and never detects revoked serials, so a revoked client certificate is accepted — an improper certificate validation (CWE-295). The fix changes the argument to `issuer`, restoring the correct lookup. The added `if (revoked == NULL) continue;` is a secondary null-guard hardening the loop.

individual_review.reason: The revocation phase looks up CRLs by the current certificate subject rather than its issuer, so the issuing CA revocation list can be missed and ok returned. The fix uses issuer for that second lookup; the earlier subject lookup intentionally verifies CRL signatures.

From af61f9fdd15cd439da9e2fe5fa39d174c923eaae Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Ignacio R. Morelle" <shadowm@wesnoth.org>
Date: Fri, 16 May 2014 01:45:18 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] fs: Use game data path to resolve ./ in the absence of a
 current_dir

Fixes a file content disclosure bug (#22042) affecting functionality
relying on the get_wml_location() function and not passing a non-empty
value for the current_dir parameter.

See <https://gna.org/bugs/?22042> for details.

This is a candidate for the 1.10 and 1.12 branches.

(Backported from master, commit 314425ab0e57b32909d324f7d4bf213d62cbd3b5.)
---
 changelog          |  1 +
 src/filesystem.cpp | 14 ++++++++++++--
 2 files changed, 13 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/changelog b/changelog
index ef1cac26c138a..9f46bdff6c45a 100644
--- a/changelog
+++ b/changelog
@@ -26,6 +26,7 @@ Version 1.10.7+dev:
      color codes as the start of a comment.
    * Fixed: Compilation with CLang 3.2 and libc++.
    * Fixed bug #20876: A segfault in cut_surface.
+   * Fix bug #22042: filesystem content disclosure issue affecting Lua APIs
 
 Version 1.10.7:
  * Add-ons server:
diff --git a/src/filesystem.cpp b/src/filesystem.cpp
index 2fa8ad5cbb601..7b4bd957ba912 100644
--- a/src/filesystem.cpp
+++ b/src/filesystem.cpp
@@ -1170,8 +1170,18 @@ std::string get_wml_location(const std::string &filename, const std::string &cur
 	else if (filename.size() >= 2 && filename[0] == '.' && filename[1] == '/')
 	{
 		// If the filename begins with a "./", look in the same directory
-		// as the file currrently being preprocessed.
-		result = current_dir + filename.substr(2);
+		// as the file currently being preprocessed.
+
+		if (!current_dir.empty())
+		{
+			result = current_dir;
+		}
+		else
+		{
+			result = game_config::path;
+		}
+
+		result += filename.substr(2);
 	}
 	else if (!game_config::path.empty())
 		result = game_config::path + "/data/" + filename;

automated_review.label: ok
automated_review.mechanism: When a filename begins with "./" and current_dir is empty, result becomes the bare filename substring, resolving relative to the process working directory rather than a controlled data dir, allowing crafted content to read arbitrary files.
automated_review.fix_evidence: if (!current_dir.empty()) { result = current_dir; } else { result = game_config::path; } result += filename.substr(2);
automated_review.reason: The ".." check blocks traversal, but with an empty current_dir the "./" branch produces a path relative to CWD (e.g. "./passwd" -> "passwd"), so a campaign/map that triggers get_wml_location with no current_dir can resolve files outside the intended game data tree, disclosing their contents; the fix substitutes game_config::path when current_dir is empty, confining resolution to the game data directory. The security effect is local to this function and matches the CVE's file-disclosure claim.

individual_review.reason: Read complete get_wml_location and full upstream fix. original_description:
CWE-732: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.
Fix commit: 9pfs: local: set the path of the export root to "."

The local backend was recently converted to using "at*()" syscalls in order
to ensure all accesses happen below the shared directory. This requires that
we only pass relative paths, otherwise the dirfd argument to the "at*()"
syscalls is ignored and the path is treated as an absolute path in the host.
This is actually the case for paths in all fids, with the notable exception
of the root fid, whose path is "/". This causes the following backend ops to
act on the "/" directory of the host instead of the virtfs shared directory
when the export root is involved:
- lstat
- chmod
- chown
- utimensat

ie, chmod /9p_mount_point in the guest will be converted to chmod / in the
host for example. This could cause security issues with a privileged QEMU.

All "*at()" syscalls are being passed an open file descriptor. In the case
of the export root, this file descriptor points to the path in the host that
was passed to -fsdev.

The fix is thus as simple as changing the path of the export root fid to be
"." instead of "/".

This is CVE-2017-7471.

original_description:
CWE-20: The product receives input or data, but it does not validate or incorrectly validates that the input has the properties that are required to process the data safely and correctly.
Fix commit: ALSA: timer: Harden slave timer list handling

A slave timer instance might be still accessible in a racy way while
operating the master instance as it lacks of locking.  Since the
master operation is mostly protected with timer->lock, we should cope
with it while changing the slave instance, too.  Also, some linked
lists (active_list and ack_list) of slave instances aren't unlinked
immediately at stopping or closing, and this may lead to unexpected
accesses.

This patch tries to address these issues.  It adds spin lock of
timer->lock (either from master or slave, which is equivalent) in a
few places.  For avoiding a deadlock, we ensure that the global
slave_active_lock is always locked at first before each timer lock.

Also, ack and active_list of slave instances are properly unlinked at
snd_timer_stop() and snd_timer_close().

Last but not least, remove the superfluous call of _snd_timer_stop()
at removing slave links.  This is a noop, and calling it may confuse
readers wrt locking.  Further cleanup will follow in a later patch.

Actually we've got reports of use-after-free by syzkaller fuzzer, and
this hopefully fixes these issues.

automated_review.reason: fopen with mode "wb" performs an open(O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC) without O_NOFOLLOW, so if an attacker with write access to the TPM state directory pre-creates tmpfile as a symlink, the open follows it and truncates/overwrites the target. automated_review.label: ok
automated_review.mechanism: The pre-fix function skips re-validation of any path prefix already stored in path_safe, so an intervening component that becomes a symlink after being cached (or was never re-checked) lets extraction proceed through a symlink to write outside the destination.
automated_review.fix_evidence:
-	pn = a->name;
-	if (archive_strlen(&(a->path_safe)) > 0) {...} ... +	restore_pwd = open(".", ...); ... +		if (chdir(head) != 0) {...} +			head = tail + 1;
automated_review.reason: The pre-fix logic lstat()s the accumulating full path but caches the previously-verified prefix in path_safe and skips re-checking it on subsequent entries. Since it never physically descends and re-verifies component-by-component relative to a stable cwd, a prefix component verified as a safe directory can later be replaced by a symlink; the cache causes that prefix to be skipped, so the symlink is not detected and the write escapes the destination (classic TOCTOU / partial-path link-following, CWE-59). The fix removes the path_safe short-circuit entirely, uses chdir() to descend into each verified directory so each subsequent lstat is on a single relative component rooted at the current (verified) directory, and restores the original cwd with fchdir(). This eliminates the cached-prefix trust and the multi-component TOCTOU window.

individual_review.reason: Read complete check_symlinks and patch. Cached path_safe prefix bypasses fresh lstat on components, allowing intervening symlink replacement to redirect later extraction; full accumulating paths also follow previously checked intermediate links. Fix removes cache and descends into checked directory components. CWE-59 accurate link-following flaw.

automated_review.mechanism: The title, description, and feed_title fields are inserted unquoted (only stfl-escaped, not shell-escaped) into a shell command line passed to /bin/sh -c, so shell metacharacters in attacker-controlled RSS fields execute arbitrary commands.

original_description:
Unspecified source label; identify the actual local flaw.
This instance (CVE-2020-15211): [{'lang': 'en', 'value': "In TensorFlow Lite before versions 1.15.4, 2.0.3, 2.1.2, 2.2.1 and 2.3.1, saved models in the flatbuffer format use a double indexing scheme: a model has a set of subgraphs, each subgraph has a set of operators and each operator has a set of input/output tensors. The flatbuffer format uses indices for the tensors, indexing into an array of tensors that is owned by the subgraph. This results in a pattern of double array indexing when trying to get the data of each tensor. However, some operators can have some tensors be optional. To handle this scenario, the flatbuffer model uses a negative `-1` value as index for these tensors. This results in special casing during validation at model loading time. Unfortunately, this means that the `-1` index is a valid tensor index for any operator, including those that don't expect optional inputs and including for output tensors. Thus, this allows writing and reading from outside the bounds of heap allocated arrays, although only at a specific offset from the start of these arrays. This results in both read and write gadgets, albeit very limited in scope. The issue is patched in several commits (46d5b0852, 00302787b7, e11f5558, cd31fd0ce, 1970c21, and fff2c83), and is released in TensorFlow versions 1.15.4, 2.0.3, 2.1.2, 2.2.1, or 2.3.1. A potential workaround would be to add a custom `Verifier` to the model loading code to ensure that only operators which accept optional inputs use the `-1` special value and only for the tensors that they expect to be optional. Since this allow-list type approach is erro-prone, we advise upgrading to the patched code."}]

The high-level libblkid API uses /run/blkid/blkid.tab cache to
store probing results. The cache format is

   <device NAME="value" ...>devname</device>

and unfortunately the cache code does not escape quotation marks:

automated_review.label: ok
automated_review.mechanism: In the do_curly quantifier handling, the multiplication minnext * mincount and its addition to min can overflow SSize_t (32-bit) when nested quantifiers produce large repeat counts, yielding a small/negative length used later for buffer sizing.
automated_review.fix_evidence: if ( ( minnext > 0 && mincount >= SSize_t_MAX / minnext ) || min >= SSize_t_MAX - minnext * mincount ) { FAIL("Regexp out of space"); }
automated_review.reason: For CURLY/PLUS/STAR nodes, mincount comes from ARG1/ARG2 (the quantifier bounds) and minnext is the recursively-studied minimum length of the loop body. With nested quantifiers such as (a{N}){M}, minnext can already be large and mincount large, so minnext*mincount and the running min accumulate without any bound check. On 32-bit SSize_t this wraps to a small or negative value; the resulting minlen feeds RExC_maxlen and downstream regex program size calculations, leading to heap buffer overflow. The added guard checks both the multiplication overflow (mincount >= SSize_t_MAX/minnext) and the addition overflow (min >= SSize_t_MAX - minnext*mincount) before performing the very computation on the following line, aborting compilation. This is exactly the CWE-190 wraparound the CVE describes, fixed in the same function containing the vulnerable expression.

individual_review.reason: Nested regex quantifier minima multiply then accumulate in SSize_t without overflow guards; inspected actual min+=minnext*mincount expression. Fix checks multiplication and addition limits first.

Subject: [PATCH] vhost: check log mmap offset and size overflow

vhost_user_set_log_base() is a message handler that is
called to handle the VHOST_USER_SET_LOG_BASE message.
Its payload contains a 64 bit size and offset. Both are
added up and used as a size when calling mmap().

There is no integer overflow check. If an integer overflow
occurs a smaller memory map would be created than
requested. Since the returned mapping is mapped as writable
and used for logging, a memory corruption could occur.

CVE-2020-10722
Fixes: fbc4d248b198 ("vhost: fix offset while mmaping log base address")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Reported-by: Ilja Van Sprundel <ivansprundel@ioactive.com>
Signed-off-by: Maxime Coquelin <maxime.coquelin@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Xiaolong Ye <xiaolong.ye@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Ilja Van Sprundel <ivansprundel@ioactive.com>

 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/lib/librte_vhost/vhost_user.c b/lib/librte_vhost/vhost_user.c
index 9c891d4c019..ff5b13169fe 100644
--- a/lib/librte_vhost/vhost_user.c
+++ b/lib/librte_vhost/vhost_user.c
@@ -2068,10 +2068,10 @@ vhost_user_set_log_base(struct virtio_net **pdev, struct VhostUserMsg *msg,
 	size = msg->payload.log.mmap_size;
 	off  = msg->payload.log.mmap_offset;
 
-	/* Don't allow mmap_offset to point outside the mmap region */
-	if (off > size) {
+	/* Check for mmap size and offset overflow. */
+	if (off >= -size) {
 		VHOST_LOG_CONFIG(ERR,
-			"log offset %#"PRIx64" exceeds log size %#"PRIx64"\n",
+			"log offset %#"PRIx64" and log size %#"PRIx64" overflow\n",

automated_review.mechanism: In the while loop, `while (*s)` dereferences `s` after it was advanced by `s += (*s)+1` without any bounds/TCHECK verification of the new position, reading past the captured buffer.
automated_review.fix_evidence: added `ND_TCHECK2(*s, 1);` after `s += (*s) + 1;` ensures the advanced pointer points to captured data before the next loop dereferences `*s`.
automated_review.reason: The loop advances `s += (*s) + 1` and then loops back to test `while (*s)`, dereferencing the new `s` at the top of the loop. The in-loop `if (s >= maxbuf)` and `ND_TCHECK2` checks occur before the increment, so after incrementing there is no validation before `while (*s)` reads the byte; with a crafted length byte `s` can jump past both maxbuf and the captured snapshot, causing an over-read. The fix adds `ND_TCHECK2(*s,1)` immediately after the increment so a truncated position triggers the trunc goto. This matches CWE-125 buffer over-read.

individual_review.reason: After advancing s by a length byte, the next while condition dereferences it before either bound check. Patch checks the advanced pointer.

automated_review.mechanism: The device volume label (externally influenced) is expanded into a command string via expandMacros without shell quoting and then passed to KRun::runCommand, which parses it as a shell command, allowing command injection through metacharacters like $() in the label.
automated_review.reason: exec is built from m_service.exec() and expanded with device attributes (including the volume label) via expandMacros, which performs no neutralization; the result is executed via KRun::runCommand which interprets it as a shell command, so a label such as "$(touch b)" runs arbitrary commands. The fix substitutes expandMacrosShellQuote, which shell-quotes the expanded values so special characters are treated literally, neutralizing the injection at the point where the command string is constructed.

individual_review.reason: Device macro values, including the volume label, are expanded into a shell command without quoting. The shell-quoting expander repairs that command construction.

automated_review.reason: In the pre-fix code, the entire buffer returned by av_bprint_get_buffer is used for inflate output (avail_out = buf_size), leaving no space reserved for the NUL terminator. After the loop, bp->str[bp->len] = 0 writes at index equal to the number of bytes written, which can be exactly the buffer end, causing a one-byte out-of-bounds write. The fix requests at least 2 bytes and sets avail_out = buf_size - 1, reserving one byte so the terminator write stays in bounds. This is a genuine local out-of-bounds write fixed within this function.

automated_review.mechanism: The 16-bit 'offset' accumulates 'ipv6_optlen(exthdr)' (up to ~2040 per option) and can wrap around past packet_len, so the loop never terminates and re-reads the same options, causing an infinite loop.
automated_review.reason: offset is a u16; with a crafted extension-header chain, repeated additions of ipv6_optlen (each up to 2040) can exceed 65535 and wrap to a small value, so 'offset <= packet_len' stays true and the while loop never exits. The bounds check 'offset + sizeof(struct ipv6_opt_hdr) > packet_len' uses the already-wrapped offset and cannot catch this. Local user opening a raw socket can supply such a packet. The fix widens offset to unsigned int and rejects when len+offset >= IPV6_MAXPLEN, preventing the wraparound and infinite loop. This matches CWE-190 integer overflow leading to DoS.

individual_review.reason: Repeated extension-length additions can wrap the u16 cursor and defeat the loop bound. Widening it and rejecting sums at IPV6_MAXPLEN prevents the wraparound.

From 0f2ff82e11c86c05d051cae32b58226392d33bbf Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eric Anholt <eric@anholt.net>
Date: Tue, 17 Jan 2017 21:42:53 +1100
Subject: [PATCH] drm/vc4: Fix an integer overflow in temporary allocation
 layout.

We copy the unvalidated ioctl arguments from the user into kernel
temporary memory to run the validation from, to avoid a race where the
user updates the unvalidate contents in between validating them and
copying them into the validated BO.

However, in setting up the layout of the kernel side, we failed to
check one of the additions (the roundup() for shader_rec_offset)
against integer overflow, allowing a nearly MAX_UINT value of
bin_cl_size to cause us to under-allocate the temporary space that we
then copy_from_user into.

Reported-by: Murray McAllister <murray.mcallister@insomniasec.com>
Signed-off-by: Eric Anholt <eric@anholt.net>
Fixes: d5b1a78a772f ("drm/vc4: Add support for drawing 3D frames.")
---
 drivers/gpu/drm/vc4/vc4_gem.c | 3 ++-
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/vc4/vc4_gem.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/vc4/vc4_gem.c
index db920771bfb564..c5fe3554858e51 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/vc4/vc4_gem.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/vc4/vc4_gem.c
@@ -594,7 +594,8 @@ vc4_get_bcl(struct drm_device *dev, struct vc4_exec_info *exec)
 					  args->shader_rec_count);
 	struct vc4_bo *bo;
 
-	if (uniforms_offset < shader_rec_offset ||
+	if (shader_rec_offset < args->bin_cl_size ||
+	    uniforms_offset < shader_rec_offset ||
 	    exec_size < uniforms_offset ||
 	    args->shader_rec_count >= (UINT_MAX /
 					  sizeof(struct vc4_shader_state)) ||

automated_review.label: ok
automated_review.mechanism: The roundup(bin_offset + args->bin_cl_size, 16) computation of shader_rec_offset can wrap around uint32_t when a near-UINT_MAX bin_cl_size is supplied, and no check validates shader_rec_offset against bin_cl_size, causing temp_size to be under-allocated while copy_from_user later writes args->bin_cl_size bytes.
automated_review.reason: The pre-fix overflow checks verify uniforms_offset < shader_rec_offset, exec_size < uniforms_offset, and temp_size < exec_size, but never check that shader_rec_offset (from roundup(bin_cl_size,16)) did not wrap below bin_cl_size. A crafted bin_cl_size near UINT_MAX makes roundup wrap to a small value; subsequent offsets and temp_size stay small and pass the checks, so drm_malloc_ab(temp_size,1) under-allocates, yet copy_from_user(bin, args->bin_cl, args->bin_cl_size) writes the full bin_cl_size into the small buffer — a heap overflow rooted in the unchecked integer overflow (CWE-190). The added check `shader_rec_offset < args->bin_cl_size` detects exactly that wraparound and aborts, matching the described fix.

individual_review.reason: roundup of near-UINT_MAX bin_cl_size wraps shader offset unnoticed by later offset checks; copy_from_user retains full bin size. Patch checks first roundup too.

automated_review.mechanism: After reading a label_len byte, the function copies label_len bytes from packet+j without verifying that j+label_len stays within length, causing an out-of-bounds read past the end of the packet buffer.
automated_review.reason: GET8 only guarantees the single length byte is in-bounds; the subsequent memcpy of label_len bytes from packet+j is bounded only against name_out (cp+label_len>=end), not against the source packet buffer. A crafted DNS packet whose final label claims up to 63 bytes but sits near the buffer end reads past packet+length. The added check `if (j + label_len > length) return -1;` bounds the source read against the packet length, directly preventing the OOB read. The removed `if (j >= length)` line is redundant with GET8's own check and is unrelated to the fix's security effect.

individual_review.reason: DNS label memcpy validates destination capacity only; source packet may contain fewer than label_len bytes. Patch checks j+label_len against packet length.

automated_review.mechanism: The function calls parse_iv2 on (*p)+2 without checking that *p+2 remains within the buffer bound (max), allowing a read past the end of the serialized data buffer when the input ends prematurely.

automated_review.reason: In PHP's unserializer, *p points into the serialized buffer and max is the buffer end (an ordinary API invariant of UNSERIALIZE_PARAMETER). The pre-fix code advances and parses at (*p)+2 without verifying at least 2 bytes remain before max, so parse_iv2 reads bytes past the buffer end for crafted truncated input. The added bounds check *p >= max - 2 rejects such input before the over-read, directly addressing the out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The return-value change to -1 propagates the error correctly.

individual_review.reason: Parsing begins at *p+2 without checking serialized-buffer end. The added max-2 guard prevents a truncated input from reaching the numeric parser outside the buffer.

The original check computes `p+l`, which for a large `l` overflows the pointer and can produce a value <= `buf+n`, passing validation. The fix rewrites the check as `l > (unsigned)(buf+n-p)`, comparing the length against the remaining bytes without computing an overflowing pointer, correctly rejecting oversized lengths. This matches CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read) and the DoS described.

The fix adds a bounds check on buffer_caret + encoded_pixels*pixel_block_size against image_block_size before the read loop, aborting on overflow. This matches CWE-125.

individual_review.reason: RLE/raw packet counts drive reads at buffer_caret+j without source-buffer bounds; patch checks packet extent before loops.

automated_review.mechanism: After dropping mmap_sem, madvise_remove uses vma->vm_file in do_fallocate without holding a reference, so a concurrent munmap/close can free the vma and its file, causing a use-after-free.
automated_review.reason: The function explicitly drops mmap_sem (*prev = NULL) before calling do_fallocate, but continues to dereference vma->vm_file after the lock is released. Once mmap_sem is dropped, a concurrent munmap or close on another thread can tear down the vma and drop the last reference to the file, so the vm_file passed to do_fallocate may already be freed — a classic race/use-after-free. The fix takes an explicit reference (get_file) before dropping the lock and uses the local pinned pointer f, then fput after fallocate, keeping the file alive across the window. The shared resource (the file/vma) and competing accessor (munmap/close) are identified, matching CWE-362.

individual_review.reason: After dropping mmap_sem, the function reads vma->vm_file without holding a file reference; concurrent unmap or close can release the VMA and file. The patch saves and references the file before unlocking, then drops that reference after fallocate.

automated_review.mechanism: In the first loop iteration, the code processes the chunk (including sctp_walk_errors over ERROR causes) before verifying that ch_end (ch + chunk length) lies within the skb tail, so a crafted chunk with a length extending past the packet buffer causes out-of-bounds reads.
automated_review.fix_evidence: Added before the type-appropriate handling: "ch_end = ((__u8 *)ch) + SCTP_PAD4(ntohs(ch->length)); if (ch_end > skb_tail_pointer(skb)) return sctp_sf_violation_chunklen(...)"
automated_review.reason: Pre-fix, the only length check inside the loop is the minimal-header check (ch->length < sizeof(sctp_chunkhdr_t)); the upper-bound check (ch_end > skb_tail_pointer) occurred only at the END of the iteration, after code already dereferenced chunk contents such as walking ERROR cause fields via sctp_walk_errors. A crafted first chunk with a large declared length that exceeds the actual skb data lets sctp_walk_errors iterate past the buffer end, reading out-of-bounds slab memory. The fix moves the ch_end bounds check to the start of each iteration, so the buffer overrun is rejected before any type-specific parsing. This is precisely CWE-125 out-of-bounds read; label matches.

individual_review.reason: SCTP error walker dereferences chunk content before upper-bound validation; patch moves chunk-end validation ahead of processing.

automated_review.reason: nvec derives from the VFIO_DEVICE_SET_IRQS ioctl count and reaches this function; the explicit multiplication in kzalloc can wrap when nvec is large, producing an undersized allocation while vdev->num_ctx is set to nvec and used for later per-vector indexing. kcalloc performs an internal overflow-checked multiply (nvec * size) and returns NULL on overflow, which the existing NULL check then handles, closing the integer-overflow path. automated_review.mechanism: OBJ_obj2txt returns the total length the textual representation would have (potentially larger than the buffer), so passing that return value to BIO_write causes reads past the end of the 128-byte obj_txt buffer.
automated_review.vulnerable_expression:
int len = OBJ_obj2txt(obj_txt, sizeof(obj_txt), obj, 0);
    BIO_write(bio, obj_txt, len);
automated_review.reason: OBJ_obj2txt's documented contract returns the number of bytes needed for the full representation, not the number actually written; the buffer is always NUL-terminated within its 128 bytes but len can exceed 128 for a large OID. BIO_write(bio, obj_txt, len) then reads len bytes from a 128-byte stack buffer, reading out of bounds. The fix discards the return value and uses BIO_printf with %s, which stops at the NUL terminator, bounding the read to the actual buffer contents. A crafted time-stamp file supplying an oversized OID triggers this.

individual_review.reason: OBJ_obj2txt returns required length, which can exceed the 128-byte output buffer. BIO_write trusts that length; switching to a terminated string bounds the actual read.
